identity.title: [v0.92][WP-18C.07] Harden and prove the Observatory as a production Polis interface

values.review_scope: Issue #117 integrated real-Runtime HTML Observatory behavior across roster, one-to-one chat, durable history, governed rooms, attention inbox, authority preservation, safe rendering, origin and token security, privacy and redaction, accessibility, responsive desktop/mobile behavior, reconnect and restart resilience, backpressure and offline degradation, version mismatch, resource bounds, operator runbook, artifact truth, rollback, terminal dependency ancestry, affected-area ownership, and exact-head product, architecture, and security review.
review_prompts: Can browser state, stale events, caches, storage, URLs, display data, optimistic updates, or reconnect buffers create identity, recipient, replay, intervention, or policy authority?

Can any Runtime, provider-derived, operator, message, room, history, inbox, refusal, diagnostic, or URL content become executable markup or leak through logs, screenshots, traces, or retained artifacts?

Are roster, chat, history, rooms, inbox, refusal, recovery, and error workflows fully keyboard operable and meaningfully exposed to assistive technology across desktop, mobile, zoom, reflow, contrast, and reduced motion?

Can loss, gaps, restart, backpressure, offline mode, version mismatch, reload, or partial degradation fabricate continuity, hide stale state, or duplicate commands, messages, receipts, unread counts, or acknowledgements?
Are every latency, memory, DOM, list, transcript, queue, stream, buffer, retry, timeout, response, screenshot, trace, and artifact bound explicit, enforced, and proven under realistic scale?
Does every claim bind to one exact real-Runtime revision after #83 and #111-#116 terminal handoff, with #122 excluded and no unresolved product, architecture, or security finding?
